zBuscaLabel: Which zone am I in? Find your municipality
mSub: We count the fire that satellites have seen since 2001 and put it on a single scale, so that each year can be compared with normal.
mFoco1: Each satellite passes over the peninsula twice a day, once by day and once by night, and marks the places where it detects the heat of a fire. We divide the map into squares, and a hot spot is a 1 km square with fire on one day: if the same square burns for three days, it counts three times.
mFoco2: The satellite sees any fire: it cannot tell a milpa burn from a wildfire. And no hot spots does not mean there was no fire, because clouds and smoke hide it and a very small fire can slip past.
mUnirTitulo: How we joined 25 years of satellites
mUnir1: Satellites were added over the years, and adding up what all of them see would inflate recent years. So we use one for each period:
mUnir2: Today's satellites (VIIRS) see smaller fires than earlier ones (MODIS). In the season, for every square with fire that Aqua saw in Yucatán, today's satellites see between {a} and {b}, depending on the zone. Using the years they flew together, we calculated a factor for each zone and time of year, and with it we brought the MODIS years to today's scale.
mGrafTitulo: Hot spots in Yucatán, March 1 to May 31 of each year
mRayas: Hatched: MODIS years brought to the VIIRS scale.
mSaltoCrudo: Without calibration, fire seems to have multiplied by {c} from {a1}–{a2} to {d1}–{d2}.
mSaltoArmonizado: Calibrated, it multiplied by {r}: the jump came from the satellite, not from the fire.
mCrudoAria: Without calibration: from 2001 to 2011 the bars stay very low and fire seems to jump in 2012.
mArmonizadoAria: With the calibration: the years from 2001 to 2011 reach the level of today's and the jump disappears.
mConfiarConafor: of the {i} fires that Mexico's National Forestry Commission (CONAFOR) recorded on the peninsula from {d} to {h} had hot spots nearby, at the place and on the dates of the fire. By chance alone, {z}% would match.
mConfiarGrandes: of the {n} fires larger than {ha} hectares also had hot spots nearby: the bigger the fire, the easier it is for the satellite to see it.
mConfiarNoaa: hot spots seen by NOAA-20 for each one seen by S-NPP in the season. Today’s satellites agree, so from {f}, when S-NPP stopped sending data, the series can continue with NOAA-20 without a jump.
mConfiarNota: CONAFOR records wildfires, not agricultural burns: this shows that the satellite sees fire, but it says nothing about burning dates.
mDescarga1: The complete harmonized series, with every week from 2001 to 2026 in {n} municipalities of the peninsula and the normal for each week. The boundaries we use do not yet include the three newest municipalities (Dzitbalché, Seybaplaya and Puerto Morelos), so their fire counts in the municipality they split from. It is a CSV table that Excel opens; the column names are in the first row.
mPie: Data: FIRMS (NASA), {a} to {b}, and CONAFOR wildfire records, {d} to {h}. Updated {f}.
mIA: We built this project with the help of artificial intelligence (Claude, by Anthropic) for research, code and drafting. The team chose the method and checked every figure against its source.
mIAEnlace: What the AI did and did not do
